confidence_notes: I based the restaurant, coffee and beer prices on one web search of cost-of-living sites (traveltables, livingcost, citycost and similar). Those sites were often out of date and disagreed with each other. So I nudged the prices up for tourist venues near White Beach and for the July 2026 window. That gives an inexpensive meal of about PHP 250-350, a cappuccino of about PHP 140 and a draft beer of about PHP 110-120 in a restaurant. A search result reported that one beach bar charged about PHP 100. I did not check cocktail or wine prices directly. I estimated them from how they usually compare with beer in Boracay's tourist bars: cocktails about 3-4x beer and wine about 3x, because imported wine costs a lot in the Philippines. All accommodation prices are my own estimates from general knowledge, not live listings. They are the least certain, and July is the wet low season, so rates may be lower than these mid-year figures. I got the FX rate from a search summary that cites the RBA's 4.00pm rate for 18 November 2026. I did not open the rba.gov.au page myself.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are set at a premium of about 20-40% over other Philippine beach destinations such as El Nido, Siargao and Panglao, and over Manila prices for food and drink. Boracay is the country's most developed resort island.
